newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Asian MP says triad problem manageable.
newsitem.headline: NZ Asian MP says triad problem manageable.

text.p: New Zealand's first Asian member of parliament said on Wednesday the problem of Asian triad gang activity was manageable if measures to prevent it were taken now.

Speaking to journalists after meeting Police Minister Jack Elder, Pansy Wong said she had no personal experience of triads operating in New Zealand and had received no complaints from constituents in the Asian community about their activities.

"I see them as organised crime activity and we must recognise it exists, and I am supporting the police call in terms of both engaging preventative measures and recruiting Asian police from overseas," Wong said.

New Zealand police and politicians are increasingly concerned about organised crime and a proliferation of gangs, citing evidence of links between triads and well-established networks like the Maori Mongrel Mob.

Opposition Labour member of parliament Phil Goff, returning from talks in Hong Kong last week, said: "The Hong Kong police acknowledge that there has been increasing infiltration of triads into New Zealand as our Asian community has grown."

He said Asian immigrants, mainly Chinese from Hong Kong, Taiwan and China, made up more than a 10th of the population in Auckland, New Zealand's biggest city, and were linked to drugs, extortion, loan shark schemes and racketeering.

Wong, who was elected as a conservative National member of parliament in last October's election, said if New Zealand moved now and took preventative measures "we are in a very good position to be positive about the future".
Elder told reporters after the meeting every immigrant group brought the benefits of its culture and some of its problems to New Zealand.
But he indicated he wanted to see a much tougher screening process once a potential immigrant's links with organised crime had been established.
"We should take the view it is our prerogative to say they do or don't come. Whether there's absolute proof present is, to my way of thinking, not an essential."
